title: The constant periodic resolution and its nonzero quotient
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $t\in R$ satisfy $t^2=0$ and $\{r\in R:tr=0\}=tR$, and put $F=R/tR$. Let $V$ be any scheme, with its small pro-etale site and size convention [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Write $R_V,F_V$ for the constant ring and module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], with the $R_V$-action on $F_V$ induced by the quotient $R\to F$. Define $P_V$ [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] by $P_V^i=R_V$ for $i\leq0$, $P_V^i=0$ for $i>0$, and differential multiplication by the constant section $t$ for $i<0$, zero otherwise. Let $\pi_V:P_V^0\to F_V$ be the constant quotient map. Then $\cdots\xrightarrow{t}R_V\xrightarrow{t}R_V\xrightarrow{\pi_V}F_V\to0$ is exact, and the map $P_V\to F_V[0]$ with degree-zero component $\pi_V$ is a K-flat resolution [def-pc-kflat-complex]. More precisely, the kernel and the image of multiplication by $t$ on $R_V$ coincide, its cokernel is canonically $F_V$, all terms of $P_V$ are flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], and multiplication by $t$ on $F_V$ is zero. If $V$ is nonempty, the canonical map from $F$ to the underlying abelian group $F_V(V)$, taking an element to its constant section, is injective. Consequently $F\ne0$ and nonempty $V$ imply $F_V\ne0$. No nonvanishing is claimed for empty $V$, and no finiteness or connectedness condition is imposed.

proof.text: Let $\mu:R\to R$ send $r$ to $tr$, and let $q:R\to F$ be the quotient. Its image is $tR$, its kernel is $tR$ by hypothesis, and $q$ is surjective with kernel $tR$. Thus $\ker\mu=\operatorname{im}\mu$ and $\operatorname{coker}\mu=F$ via $q$. Also $\mu^2(r)=t^2r=0$ and $t\bar r=\overline{tr}=0$ in $F$. These calculations include the zero ring.

proof.text: Work on the small site fixed by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $C$ be the constant module functor of [def-sf-site-constant-module-functor]. Its prescribed constant scalar action identifies $C(R)$ with $R_V$, $C(F)$ with $F_V$, $C(\mu)$ with multiplication by the constant $t$, and $C(q)$ with $\pi_V$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-constant-exact] with the commutative ring $R$: it preserves kernels and cokernels. It also preserves images, since $\operatorname{im} f=\ker(\operatorname{coker} f)$. Applying this to step 1 gives $\ker(\mu_t)=\operatorname{im}(\mu_t)$ and the canonical identification $\operatorname{coker}(\mu_t)\cong F_V$, with quotient map $\pi_V$. The same constant scalar construction sends the zero scalar endomorphism of $F$ to zero on $F_V$, so $tF_V=0$; it sends $t^2=0$ to $\mu_t^2=0$.

Apply [lem-sfb-exact-scalar-periodic-resolution] on this small site with $\mathcal O=R_V$ and $t_U$ the constant section $t$ on each object $U$. These sections are restriction-compatible and square to zero; step 2 verifies its kernel-equals-image hypothesis. Under its canonical cokernel identification $E\cong F_V$, its complex is precisely $P_V$ and its augmentation has degree-zero component $\pi_V$. The cited statement therefore gives exactness of the entire augmented sequence, flatness of every term, and that this augmentation is a K-flat resolution. In particular the zero cutoff is in degree $0$, not a lower bound on the complex.

proof.text: Assume $V$ is nonempty and let $a,b\in F$ have the same constant section in $F_V(V)$. Apply local injectivity of the unit in [lem-sf-constant-module-unit-locally-bijective] to $M=F$ over $R$: there is a covering family $\{U_i\to V\}$ on which $a$ and $b$ have equal restrictions in the constant presheaf itself. By the covering condition in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], this family has a nonempty member: choose a point of $V$ and an affine neighborhood of it, and one of the finitely many covering affine opens whose image contains that point. On its containing $U_i$, restriction in the constant presheaf is the identity of $F$, so the equality is $a=b$. Thus $F\to F_V(V)$ is injective.

No new nodes, no changes to the statement, and no Lean edits or compilation.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q33-d125f3c1d (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read in full: the item's 5 steps, every cited statement, Stacks 093J/03CY/06YQ at their labels, and the blueprint ctf-equals-bc 'The examples'. No new nodes and no re-split note. The statement is byte-identical to Q43's creation; the only stmt_dep added is def-sf-site-constant-module-functor, which defines the constant-module action the statement uses. Step 1: ker t = Ann(t) = tR = im t, coker = F via q; elementary. Step 2: C from def-sf-site-constant-module-functor gives R_V, F_V, mult-by-t and pi_V. lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-constant-exact preserves kernels and cokernels over any ring with no finiteness hypotheses, so it also preserves images, giving ker = im on R_V, coker = F_V and tF_V = 0. Its functor (termwise sheafification of constant presheaves) is the same construction as C; advisory. Step 3: every hypothesis of lem-sfb-exact-scalar-periodic-resolution is met (small site, compatible square-zero t, ker = im) and degree conventions match; that node is unsplit, so no cycle. Step 4: local injectivity of the unit for M = F plus the pro-etale covering condition (a nonempty affine forces a nonempty member) and identity restrictions give a = b. Step 5: elementary. Edge cases: R = 0 fine; t = 0 with R nonzero is excluded, as it must be; Z/4 with t = 2 and k[e]/e^2 hold; Z/8 with t = 4 correctly excluded; V empty is handled. No SGA. Duplicate search found only the general scalar node (cited) and the unrelated cyclic-group resolution. Tool uses of the two generic sheafification lemmas are accepted.
